q: Deciding the matter by their superior knowledge, (the Tîrthakaras) have fixed what is necessary for carrying out the Law.

s: the Tîrthakaras introduce outward marks (for recognition and religious usefulness)
q: The various outward marks (of religious men) have been introduced in order that people might recognise them as such; the reason for the characteristic marks is their usefulness for religious life and their distinguishing character.

s: knowledge, faith, and right conduct are causes of final liberation (true causes)
q: Now the opinion (of the Tîrthakaras) is that knowledge, faith. and right conduct are the true causes of final liberation, (and not the outward marks).

s: Self is the one invincible foe
q: Self is the one invincible foe, (together with the four) cardinal passions, (viz. anger, pride, deceit, and greed, they are five) and the (five) senses (make ten).

s: four cardinal passions are four (anger, pride, deceit, and greed)
q: Self is the one invincible foe, (together with the four) cardinal passions, (viz. anger, pride, deceit, and greed, they are five) and the (five) senses (make ten).

s: senses are five (foes)
q: Self is the one invincible foe, (together with the four) cardinal passions, (viz. anger, pride, deceit, and greed, they are five) and the (five) senses (make ten).

s: the ten foes include Self (one of ten foes)
q: Self is the one invincible foe, (together with the four) cardinal passions, (viz. anger, pride, deceit, and greed, they are five) and the (five) senses (make ten).

s: the ten foes include four cardinal passions (four of ten foes)
q: Self is the one invincible foe, (together with the four) cardinal passions, (viz. anger, pride, deceit, and greed, they are five) and the (five) senses (make ten).

s: Pârsva is a prophet of the Law
q: There was a Gina, Pârsva by name, an Arhat, worshipped by the people, who was thoroughly enlightened and omniscient, a prophet of the Law, and a Gina.

s: the ten foes include senses (five of ten foes)
q: Self is the one invincible foe, (together with the four) cardinal passions, (viz. anger, pride, deceit, and greed, they are five) and the (five) senses (make ten).

s: Gautama has vanquished the ten foes (regularly)
q: These (foes), O great sage, I have regularly vanquished.

s: fetters include love, hatred, &c. (heavy fetters)
q: Love, hatred, &c., are heavy fetters, attachment is a dangerous one; having regularly destroyed them, I live up to the rules of conduct.

s: Gautama has destroyed fetters (regularly)
q: Love, hatred, &c., are heavy fetters, attachment is a dangerous one; having regularly destroyed them, I live up to the rules of conduct.

s: love of existence is a dreadful plant (brings forth dreadful fruit)
q: Love of existence is that dreadful plant which brings forth dreadful fruit; having regularly torn it out, I live pleasantly.

s: Gautama has torn out love of existence (with its roots)
q: Love of existence is that dreadful plant which brings forth dreadful fruit; having regularly torn it out, I live pleasantly.

s: the fire of the passions is extinguished by knowledge, a virtuous life, and penances (sprinkled with the drops of knowledge)
q: The passions are the fire; knowledge, a virtuous life, and penances are the water; sprinkled with the drops of knowledge the fire of the passions is extinguished and does not burn me.

s: knowledge, virtuous life, and penances are water (extinguishes the fire of the passions)
q: The passions are the fire; knowledge, a virtuous life, and penances are the water; sprinkled with the drops of knowledge the fire of the passions is extinguished and does not burn me.

s: the mind is that unruly, dreadful, bad horse
q: The mind is that unruly, dreadful, bad horse; I govern it by the discipline of the Law (so that it becomes a well-) trained Kambôga-steed.

s: Gautama governs the mind (by the discipline of the Law)
q: The mind is that unruly, dreadful, bad horse; I govern it by the discipline of the Law (so that it becomes a well-) trained Kambôga-steed.

s: Kêsi is a young Sramana
q: And there was a famous disciple of this Light of the World, the young Sramana Kêsi, who had completely mastered the sciences and right conduct.

s: the right path is taught by Ginas (most excellent path)
q: The heterodox and the heretics have all chosen a wrong path; the right path is that taught by the Ginas; it is the most excellent path.

s: the flood of old age and death carries away living beings
q: The flood is old age and death, which carry away living beings; Law is the island, the firm ground, the refuge, the most excellent shelter.

s: the Law as refuge is the island (firm ground and most excellent shelter)
q: The flood is old age and death, which carry away living beings; Law is the island, the firm ground, the refuge, the most excellent shelter.

s: body is the boat
q: The body is the boat, life is the sailor, and the Circle of Births is the ocean which is crossed by the great sages.

s: life is the sailor
q: The body is the boat, life is the sailor, and the Circle of Births is the ocean which is crossed by the great sages.

s: Circle of Births is the ocean (crossed by the great sages)
q: The body is the boat, life is the sailor, and the Circle of Births is the ocean which is crossed by the great sages.

s: the omniscient Gina has ended Circle of Births (brings light into the whole world of living beings)
q: Risen has he who put an end to the Circle of Births, the omniscient Gina, the luminary, who brings light into the whole world of living beings.

s: Nirvâna is freedom from pain
q: It is what is called Nirvâna, or freedom from pain, or perfection, which is in view of all; it is the safe, happy, and quiet place which the great sages reach.

s: Kêsi is a disciple of Pârsva (famous disciple)
q: And there was a famous disciple of this Light of the World, the young Sramana Kêsi, who had completely mastered the sciences and right conduct.

s: Nirvâna is perfection
q: It is what is called Nirvâna, or freedom from pain, or perfection, which is in view of all; it is the safe, happy, and quiet place which the great sages reach.

s: Kêsi adopts the five vows (sincerely, according to the teaching of the last Tîrthakara)
q: And in the pleasant (Tinduka park) he sincerely adopted the Law of the five vows, which was proclaimed by the first Tîrthakara, according to the teaching of the last Tîrthakara.

s: the meeting of Kêsi and Gautama brings to eminence knowledge (for ever)
q: In that meeting of Kêsi and Gautama, knowledge and virtuous conduct were for ever brought to eminence, and subjects of the greatest importance were settled.

s: the meeting of Kêsi and Gautama brings to eminence virtuous conduct (for ever)
q: In that meeting of Kêsi and Gautama, knowledge and virtuous conduct were for ever brought to eminence, and subjects of the greatest importance were settled.

s: Kêsi has mastered the sciences (completely)
q: And there was a famous disciple of this Light of the World, the young Sramana Kêsi, who had completely mastered the sciences and right conduct.

s: Kêsi has mastered right conduct (completely)
q: And there was a famous disciple of this Light of the World, the young Sramana Kêsi, who had completely mastered the sciences and right conduct.

s: Kêsi possesses Sruta knowledge
q: He possessed the light of Sruta and Avadhi knowledge, and was surrounded by a crowd of disciples; wandering from village to village he arrived in the town of Srâvastî.

s: Twenty-Fourth Lecture is a lecture
q: Twenty-Fourth Lecture.

s: ukkâra-samiti is a Samiti (performing the operations of nature in an unfrequented place)
q: 5. ukkâra-samiti (performing the operations of nature in an unfrequented place).

s: mano-gupti is a Gupti (preventing the mind from wandering in sensual pleasures through contemplation, study, and similar practices)
q: 1. mano-gupti (preventing the mind from wandering in the forest of sensual pleasures by employing it in contemplation, study, &c.);

s: vâg-gupti is a Gupti (preventing the tongue from saying bad things through silence and similar practices)
q: 2. vâg-gupti (preventing the tongue from saying bad things by a vow of silence, &c.);

s: kâya-gupti is a Gupti (putting the body in an immovable posture as in Kâyôtsarga)
q: 3. kâya-gupti (putting the body in an immovable posture as in the case of Kâyôtsarga). (2)

s: five Samitis comprehend creed (the whole creed taught by the Ginas and set forth in the twelve Aṅgas)
q: The eight Samitis are thus briefly enumerated, in which the whole creed taught by the Ginas and set forth in the twelve Aṅgas, is comprehended. (3)

s: walking is a practice of a well-disciplined monk (pure in four respects)
q: The walking of a well-disciplined monk should be pure in four respects: in respect to 1. the cause; 2. the time; 3. the road; 4. the effort. (4)

s: walking requires knowledge, faith, and right conduct (as its cause)
q: The cause is: knowledge, faith, and right conduct; the time is day-time; the road excludes bad ways. (5)

s: walking occurs at day-time (as its proper time)
q: The cause is: knowledge, faith, and right conduct; the time is day-time; the road excludes bad ways. (5)

s: walking excludes bad ways (as its road)
q: The cause is: knowledge, faith, and right conduct; the time is day-time; the road excludes bad ways. (5)

s: monks walks carefully walking (by attending only to his walk and body, avoiding sense objects, and minding his study)
q: He walks carefully who pays attention only to his walk and his body (executing it), whilst he avoids attending to the objects of sense, but (minds) his study, the latter in all five ways. (8)

s: five Samitis are part of creed (as eight articles)
q: The eight articles of the creed are the Samitis and the Guptis; there are five Samitis and three Guptis. (1)

s: monks uses blameless and concise speech (at the proper time)
q: he should use blameless and concise speech at the proper time. (9, 10)

s: begging has objects food, articles of use, and lodging (three kinds of objects)
q: As regards begging, a monk should avoid the faults in the search, in the receiving, and in the use of the three kinds of objects, viz. food, articles of use, and lodging. (11)

s: monks avoids faults in begging (in searching, receiving, and using food, articles of use, and lodging)
q: As regards begging, a monk should avoid the faults in the search, in the receiving, and in the use of the three kinds of objects, viz. food, articles of use, and lodging. (11)

s: monks uses general and supplementary outfit (after inspecting and wiping each thing before taking it up or putting it down)
q: If a monk takes up or lays down the two kinds of things belonging to his general and supplementary outfit, he should proceed in the following way. (13) A zealous monk should wipe the thing after having inspected it with his eyes, and then he should take it up or put it down, having the Samiti in both respects. (I 4)

s: mano-gupti prevents sinful thoughts (including desires for another's misfortune and thoughts causing misery or destruction to living beings)
q: A zealous monk should prevent his mind from desires for the misfortune of somebody else, from thoughts on acts which cause misery to living beings, and from thoughts on acts which cause their destruction. (21)

s: vâg-gupti prevents sinful speech (including expressions of desires and thoughts causing misery or destruction to living beings)
q: A zealous monk should prevent his speech from (expressing) desires, &c. (as in verse 21). (23)

s: kâya-gupti prevents sinful bodily conduct (in standing, sitting, lying down, jumping, going, and using the organs)
q: In standing, sitting, lying down, jumping, going, and in the use of his organs, a zealous monk should prevent his body from intimating obnoxious desires, from doing acts which cause misery to living beings, or which cause their destruction. (24, 25)

s: religious exercise has practices five Samitis (for practice)
q: These are the five Samitis for the practice of the religious life, and the Guptis for the prevention of everything sinful. (26)

s: religious exercise has practices Guptis (for preventing everything sinful)
q: These are the five Samitis for the practice of the religious life, and the Guptis for the prevention of everything sinful. (26)

s: Guptis are part of creed (as eight articles)
q: The eight articles of the creed are the Samitis and the Guptis; there are five Samitis and three Guptis. (1)

s: monks practices five Samitis (as the essence of the creed)
q: This is the essence of the creed, which a sage should thoroughly put into practice; such a wise man will soon get beyond the Circle of Births. (27)

s: monks practices Guptis (as the essence of the creed)
q: This is the essence of the creed, which a sage should thoroughly put into practice; such a wise man will soon get beyond the Circle of Births. (27)

s: Circle of Births is exceeded by wise man (through thorough practice of the creed)
q: This is the essence of the creed, which a sage should thoroughly put into practice; such a wise man will soon get beyond the Circle of Births. (27)

s: five Samitis has count five
q: The eight articles of the creed are the Samitis and the Guptis; there are five Samitis and three Guptis. (1)

s: Guptis has count three
q: The eight articles of the creed are the Samitis and the Guptis; there are five Samitis and three Guptis. (1)

s: îryâ-samiti is a Samiti (going by paths trodden by men, beasts, carts, &c., and looking carefully so as not to occasion the death of any living creature)
q: The Samitis are: 1. îryâ-samiti (going by paths trodden by men, beasts, carts, &c., and looking carefully so as not to occasion the death of any living creature);

s: bhâshâ-samiti is a Samiti (gentle, salutary, sweet, righteous speech)
q: 2. bhâshâ-samiti (gentle, salutary, sweet, righteous speech);

s: êshanâ-samiti is a Samiti (receiving alms while avoiding forty-two faults)
q: 3. êshanâ-samiti (receiving alms in a manner to avoid the forty-two faults that are laid down);

s: âdâna-samiti is a Samiti (receiving and keeping necessary religious articles after careful examination)
q: 4. âdâna-samiti (receiving and keeping of the things necessary for religious exercises, after having carefully examined them);

s: Gayaghôsha is a Brâhmana (famous sage)
q: There was a famous Brâhmana, Gayaghôsha by name, who was born in a Brâhmanical family, but who was pledged to the performing of the yamas.

s: Gayaghôsha rejects any alms
q: I do not want any alms; but, O Brâhmana, enter the order at once, lest you should be drifted about on the dreadful ocean of the Samsâra, whose eddies are dangers.

s: Vigayaghôsha is a Brâhmana (versed in the Vêdas)
q: At the same time a Brâhmana, versed in the Vêdas, Vigayaghôsha by name, offered a sacrifice in that town.

s: Vigayaghôsha offers sacrifice (in Benares)
q: At the same time a Brâhmana, versed in the Vêdas, Vigayaghôsha by name, offered a sacrifice in that town.

s: Vigayaghôsha is a priest
q: The priest wanted to turn the approaching monk off: 'I shall not give you alms, mendicant, beg somewhere else.

s: Vigayaghôsha enters the monastic order (after learning the excellent Law)
q: When Vigayaghôsha had learned the excellent Law from the houseless Gayaghôsha, he entered the order.

s: Vigayaghôsha annihilates Karman (by self-control and penance)
q: Gayaghôsha and Vigayaghôsha both annihilated their Karman by self-control and penance, and reached the highest perfection.

s: Vigayaghôsha reaches the highest perfection (after annihilating Karman)
q: Gayaghôsha and Vigayaghôsha both annihilated their Karman by self-control and penance, and reached the highest perfection.

s: the Vêdas has essential subject agnihôtra (most essential subject)
q: The most essential subject in the Vêdas is the agnihôtra, and that of the sacrifice is the purpose of the sacrifice; the first of the heavenly bodies is the moon, and the best of dharmas is that of Kâsyapa (i.e. Rishabha).

s: sacrifice has essential subject the purpose of the sacrifice (most essential subject)
q: The most essential subject in the Vêdas is the agnihôtra, and that of the sacrifice is the purpose of the sacrifice; the first of the heavenly bodies is the moon, and the best of dharmas is that of Kâsyapa (i.e. Rishabha).

s: Gayaghôsha is born in Brâhmanical family
q: There was a famous Brâhmana, Gayaghôsha by name, who was born in a Brâhmanical family, but who was pledged to the performing of the yamas.

s: Law has best form that of Kâsyapa (i.e. Rishabha)
q: The most essential subject in the Vêdas is the agnihôtra, and that of the sacrifice is the purpose of the sacrifice; the first of the heavenly bodies is the moon, and the best of dharmas is that of Kâsyapa (i.e. Rishabha).

s: Brâhmana is one without worldly attachment (after entering the order)
q: He who has no worldly attachment after entering the order, who does not repent of having become a monk, and who takes delight in the noble words, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana is chaste (exempt from love, hatred, and fear)
q: He who is exempt from love, hatred, and fear, (and who shines forth) like burnished gold, purified in fire, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana is self_subduing ascetic (lean and pious, having reached Nirvâna)
q: A lean, self-subduing ascetic, who reduces his flesh and blood, who is pious and has reached Nirvâna, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana does not injure living beings (in any of the three ways)
q: He who thoroughly knows living beings, whether they move or not, and does not injure them in any of the three ways, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana does not speak untruth (from anger, fun, greed, or fear)
q: He who does not speak untruth from anger or for fun, from greed or from fear, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana does not take anything not given (whether sentient or not sentient, small or large)
q: He who does not take anything that is not given him, be it sentient or not sentient, small or large, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana does not carnally love divine, human, or animal beings (in thoughts, words, or acts)
q: He who does not carnally love divine, human, or animal beings, in thoughts, words, or acts, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Gayaghôsha is pledged to the yamas
q: There was a famous Brâhmana, Gayaghôsha by name, who was born in a Brâhmanical family, but who was pledged to the performing of the yamas.

s: Brâhmana is not defiled by pleasures (like a lotus growing in water)
q: He who is not defiled by pleasures as a lotus growing in the water is not wetted by it, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana lives unknown (without greed, house, or property)
q: He who is not greedy, who lives unknown, who has no house and no property, and who has no friendship with householders, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana has no friendship with householders
q: He who is not greedy, who lives unknown, who has no house and no property, and who has no friendship with householders, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana gives up former connections (with parents, kinsmen, and relations)
q: He who has given up his former connections (with his parents, &c.), with his kinsmen and relations, and who is not given to pleasure, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: Brâhmana is not given to pleasures
q: He who has given up his former connections (with his parents, &c.), with his kinsmen and relations, and who is not given to pleasure, him we call a Brâhmana.

s: sacrifice cannot save the sinner (because animal binding, the Vêdas, and sacrifices cause sin)
q: The binding of animals (to the sacrificial pole), all the Vêdas, and sacrifices, being causes of sin, cannot save the sinner; for his works (or Karman) are very powerful.

s: the Vêdas cause sin (when relied on as sacrifices)
q: The binding of animals (to the sacrificial pole), all the Vêdas, and sacrifices, being causes of sin, cannot save the sinner; for his works (or Karman) are very powerful.

s: the monastic order confers Sramana status (through equanimity)
q: One becomes a Sramana by equanimity, a Brâhmana by chastity, a Muni by knowledge, and a Tâpasa by penance.

s: Brâhmana is attained by chastity
q: One becomes a Sramana by equanimity, a Brâhmana by chastity, a Muni by knowledge, and a Tâpasa by penance.

s: Brâhmana is determined by actions (rather than birth or designation)
q: By one's actions one becomes a Brâhmana, or a Kshattriya, or a Vaisya, or a Sûdra.

s: Gayaghôsha subdues all his senses (thoroughly)
q: This great sage, who subdued all his senses, and who walked on the right road, came, on his wandering from village to village, to the town of Benares.

s: Brâhmana is exempt from all Karman
q: The Enlightened One has declared these (good qualities) through which one becomes a (true) Snâtaka; him who is exempt from all Karman, we call a Brâhmana.

s: Karman is very powerful (as the cause preventing salvation)
q: The binding of animals (to the sacrificial pole), all the Vêdas, and sacrifices, being causes of sin, cannot save the sinner; for his works (or Karman) are very powerful.

s: pleasures contains glue (as it were)
q: There is glue (as it were) in pleasure: those who are not given to pleasure, are not soiled by it; those who love pleasures, must wander about in the Samsâra; those who do not, will be liberated.

s: pleasures binds to Samsâra (through attachment)
q: There is glue (as it were) in pleasure: those who are not given to pleasure, are not soiled by it; those who love pleasures, must wander about in the Samsâra; those who do not, will be liberated.

s: Samsâra is dreadful ocean (whose eddies are dangers)
q: I do not want any alms; but, O Brâhmana, enter the order at once, lest you should be drifted about on the dreadful ocean of the Samsâra, whose eddies are dangers.

s: Samsâra is escaped by those who do not love pleasures (through liberation)
q: There is glue (as it were) in pleasure: those who are not given to pleasure, are not soiled by it; those who love pleasures, must wander about in the Samsâra; those who do not, will be liberated.

s: Karman is annihilated by tapas (together with penance)
q: Gayaghôsha and Vigayaghôsha both annihilated their Karman by self-control and penance, and reached the highest perfection.

s: Karman is annihilated by righteousness (together with self-control)
q: Gayaghôsha and Vigayaghôsha both annihilated their Karman by self-control and penance, and reached the highest perfection.

s: the highest perfection is reached by Gayaghôsha (through self-control and penance)
q: Gayaghôsha and Vigayaghôsha both annihilated their Karman by self-control and penance, and reached the highest perfection.

s: Gayaghôsha is a monk (houseless)
q: Now this houseless (monk) at the end of a fast of a month's duration, went to the sacrifice of Vigayaghôsha to beg alms.

s: the highest perfection is reached by Vigayaghôsha (through self-control and penance)
q: Gayaghôsha and Vigayaghôsha both annihilated their Karman by self-control and penance, and reached the highest perfection.

s: Gayaghôsha resides in Benares (in a pleasant park outside the town)
q: There outside of Benares he took up his lodgings in a pleasant park; there he took up his abode in a pure place to live and sleep in.

s: Gayaghôsha fasts for a month
q: Now this houseless (monk) at the end of a fast of a month's duration, went to the sacrifice of Vigayaghôsha to beg alms.

s: Gayaghôsha seeks the highest good (without anger or pleasure at refusal)
q: When the great sage was thus refused by the priest, he was neither angry nor pleased, as he always strove for the highest good.

s: Gayaghôsha speaks the following words (to save these people)
q: Not to obtain food, or drink, or whatever else he wanted, but to save these people he spoke the following words:

s: correct behaviour is a behaviour (correct)
q: The Correct Behaviour.

s: Paurushî divides day (into four equal parts)
q: A clever monk should divide the day into four (equal) parts (called paurushî), and fulfil his duties (uttaraguna) in all four parts. (11)

s: Paurushî divides night (into four parts)
q: A clever monk should divide the night too into four parts, and fulfil his duties (uttaraguna) in all four parts. (17)
